rows.grounds: those to whom one becomes dear

items.question: What attainment makes a practitioner dear to the yoginīs?
premises: Enjoyment and liberation can be attained together
This attainment constitutes a great accomplishment
Such accomplishment brings favor with the yoginīs
items.inference: One who attains the great accomplishment of enjoyment and liberation becomes dear to the yoginīs
items.plain_english: He may become dear to the yoginīs through the great accomplishment of both enjoyment and liberation.

items.question: Which chapter emerges in the context of Candra-dvīpa?
premises: A chapter is identified by its ordinal position
This chapter is said to have emerged in Candra-dvīpa
The ordinal position given is ninth
items.inference: The ninth chapter is the one that emerged in Candra-dvīpa
items.plain_english: The ninth chapter, emerged in Candra-dvīpa.

items.question: In what posture and condition is the self to be visualized?
premises: The self is described as surrounded by fire
The self is described as standing
The standing is supported on one foot
items.inference: The self is to be visualized standing on one foot while surrounded by fire
items.plain_english: Visualize the self surrounded by fire, standing on one foot.

items.question: What has been revealed to the speaker by the divine addressee?
premises: The speaker addresses a god
Something concerning knowledge has been made manifest
This manifestation has occurred today for the speaker
items.inference: The determination of knowledge has been made manifest to the speaker today by the god
items.plain_english: O God, today the determination of knowledge has been made manifest to me.

items.question: What division does the speaker seek to understand completely and without limit?
premises: There is a division of eight octads
The speaker seeks to know this division fully
The knowing is sought in an endless manner
items.inference: The speaker seeks to know fully and endlessly the division of the eight octads
items.plain_english: And to know fully and endlessly the division of the eight octads.

items.question: How are the secret place and the wheel quickly accomplished according to Bhairava?
premises: A secret place is mentioned
A wheel is mentioned
The question concerns their quick accomplishment
items.inference: The inquiry seeks the method by which the secret place and wheel are quickly accomplished
items.plain_english: O Bhairava, tell me how the secret place and the wheel are quickly accomplished.

items.question: Why does Bhairava commend the Great Goddess for her inquiry?
premises: Bhairava expresses strong approval
The Great Goddess has asked him a question
The matter asked about is hard for even gods to obtain
items.inference: Bhairava commends the Great Goddess because she has asked about something rare even for the gods
items.plain_english: Well said, well said, O Great Goddess! You have asked me about something hard for even the gods to obtain.

items.question: Which seed syllables are assigned to the brahmarandhra and the forehead?
premises: The syllable kṣa is associated with the brahmarandhra
The syllable laṃ is associated with the forehead
These are specific locational assignments
items.inference: The syllable kṣa belongs to the brahmarandhra and the syllable laṃ belongs to the forehead
uncertainties: lalāṭayoḥ is dual in form though often used for the forehead region
items.plain_english: The syllable kṣa is in the brahmarandhra, and the syllable laṃ is in the forehead.

items.question: Which seed syllables are assigned to the throat region and the heart?
premises: The syllable ṣa is placed in the throat region
The syllable śa is placed in the heart
These assignments are given as part of the same mapping
items.inference: The syllable ṣa belongs to the throat region and the syllable śa belongs to the heart
items.plain_english: Then the syllable ṣa is in the throat region, and the syllable śa is in the heart.

items.question: What does Bhairava invite the beloved to hear after declaring the place-wheels?
premises: The place-wheels have been declared
These wheels have an associated meditation
The beloved is commanded to listen
items.inference: After declaring the place-wheels, Bhairava invites the beloved to hear their meditation
items.plain_english: Thus the place-wheels have been declared; now hear their meditation, O beloved.

items.question: How is the divine lotus of the first octad to be visualized?
premises: The lotus is described as divine
The lotus has eight spokes or petals
The lotus is adorned by the first octad
items.inference: The meditation envisions a divine eight-spoked lotus adorned by the first octad
uncertainties: āra can mean spoke; in lotus imagery it may imply petals
items.plain_english: Visualize a divine eight-spoked lotus adorned by the first octad.

items.question: What conduct should a practitioner adopt after gaining mental equanimity through practice?
premises: Practice leads to an equal or balanced mind
Village dharma is presented as something to be left behind
The practitioner is instructed to abandon it
items.inference: One who has gained mental equanimity through practice should abandon village dharma
uncertainties: grāma-dharma may refer to conventional social or household duties
items.plain_english: Through practice, with mind made even, one should abandon the ways of ordinary village life.

items.question: What powers arise in connection with the first octad's practice?
premises: Knowledge of hearing distant things is mentioned
Paralysis of bonds is mentioned
These are presented together as attained results
items.inference: The practice yields knowledge of distant hearing and the power to paralyze bonds
uncertainties: pāśa-stobha could mean arresting or immobilizing bonds
items.plain_english: O beloved, one gains knowledge of hearing from afar and likewise the power to paralyze bonds.

items.question: What further results are briefly attributed to this practice?
premises: Immortality is named as a result
Transformation is named as a result
The teaching is given in brief
items.inference: In brief, the practice yields immortality and transformation
uncertainties: parivartanam may refer to bodily or experiential transformation
items.plain_english: Likewise, O Goddess, in brief, one attains immortality and transformation.

items.question: How is the second eight-petaled lotus characterized in meditation?
premises: A second lotus is introduced
It has eight petals
It is well illuminated by meditation on fire or radiance
items.inference: The second eight-petaled lotus is brilliantly illuminated through fiery meditation
uncertainties: teja may mean fire or radiant energy
items.plain_english: The second is an eight-petaled lotus, well illuminated by meditation on fiery radiance.

items.question: What ability arises for one whose mind is absorbed in one-pointed meditation?
premises: The mind becomes one-pointed in meditation
From this state an action of forming occurs
The form can be produced in many ways
items.inference: One whose mind is absorbed in one-pointed meditation can assume forms in many ways
items.plain_english: One whose mind is absorbed in one-pointed meditation can create forms in many ways.

items.question: What destructive power is attributed to the practitioner when angered?
premises: The practitioner is described as angry
The action is destruction or withdrawal
The scope includes the entire triple world, moving and unmoving
items.inference: When angered, the practitioner may destroy the entire triple world with all moving and unmoving beings
items.plain_english: When angry, he can destroy the entire triple world, with all that moves and does not move.

items.question: What liberating function is attributed to the third great wheel?
premises: A third great wheel is introduced
It is described as a liberator
Its scope is the nine principles
items.inference: The third great wheel functions as the liberator from the nine principles
uncertainties: nava-tattva may refer to a specific set of nine principles in this system
items.plain_english: The third is the great wheel, the liberator from the nine principles.

items.question: What bodily and perceptual benefits result from this wheel's practice?
premises: Destruction of wrinkles and grey hair is mentioned
Seeing from very far away is mentioned
Both are presented as attained results
items.inference: The practice removes wrinkles and grey hair and grants vision from very far away
items.plain_english: It brings the destruction of wrinkles and grey hair, and likewise the ability to see from very far away.

items.question: How should a devoted practitioner cultivate multiple forms in meditation?
premises: The practice is to be done in solitude
The practitioner should be intent on meditation
The practitioner is instructed to make forms in many ways
items.inference: A practitioner intent on meditation should, in solitude, create forms in many ways
items.plain_english: In solitude, intent on meditation, create forms in many ways.

items.question: What result comes to one devoted to constant practice?
premises: The practitioner is intent on constant practice
Immortality is named as the result
The statement presents this as a certain outcome
items.inference: One devoted to constant practice attains immortality
items.plain_english: Indeed, one who is devoted to constant practice attains immortality.

items.question: How does abstaining from eating by day affect death from aging?
premises: Non-eating by day is specified
Death associated with age is the target
The practitioner will go beyond or overcome it
items.inference: Through abstaining from eating by day, one will overcome death from aging
uncertainties: nāśanena may mean fasting or abstention from food
items.plain_english: By abstaining from food during the day, one will overcome death from aging.

items.question: What bodily form results from constant yogic practice over time?
premises: The means is constant practice through yoga
A specific age-form is indicated as sixteen years
This becomes the practitioner's form
items.inference: Through constant yogic practice, one may attain the form of a sixteen-year-old
uncertainties: dvi-aṣṭa-varṣa-ākṛtiḥ is interpreted as the form of sixteen years
items.plain_english: Through constant yogic practice, one may attain the form of a sixteen-year-old.

items.question: What power arises from continually contemplating a smoke-colored form?
premises: The practitioner is instructed to contemplate a smoke-colored form always
The triple world is named as the object affected
The resulting action is shaking or causing to tremble
items.inference: By always contemplating a smoke-colored form, one may shake the triple world
items.plain_english: O beloved, by always contemplating a smoke-colored form, one can shake the triple world.
